title: Robin's Inequality and Superabundant Counterexamples
summary: Robin's criterion states that the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $\sigma(n) 5040$. Let $n'$ be the squarefree kernel of $n$, $p_{k}$ its largest prime factor, and $d = e^{\gamma}/\zeta(2) \approx 1.08276$. We prove that Robin's inequality holds for every $n > 5040$ with $d \cdot \log\log n' \leq \log\log n$, and for every $n > 5040$ whose prime factors are all below $(\log n)^{1/d}$, and that both results remain valid with $d$ replaced by $1.016$.
